sanskrit: vipranaṣṭāś ca te 'nyonyaṃ nājānanta tadā vibho krośantas tāta putreti daivopahatacetasaḥ
english: Scattered and lost, O lord, they no longer recognized one another then; their wits struck down by fate, they cried out, "Father!" and "Son!"

sanskrit: palāyatāṃ diśas teṣāṃ svān apy utsṛjya bāndhavān gotranāmabhir anyonyam ākrandanta tato janāḥ
english: As they fled in all directions, abandoning even their own kinsmen, the men wailed to one another by their clan-names and personal names.

sanskrit: hāhākāraṃ ca kurvāṇāḥ pṛthivyāṃ śerate pare tān buddhvā raṇamatto 'sau droṇaputro vyapothayat
english: Others, raising cries of woe, lay sprawled upon the ground; and that son of Droṇa, drunk with battle, marked them out and crushed them.

sanskrit: tatrāpare vadhyamānā muhur muhur acetasaḥ śibirān niṣpatanti sma kṣatriyā bhayapīḍitāḥ
english: There still other kṣatriyas, struck down again and again and senseless, came rushing out from the camp, tormented by fear.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu niṣpatatas trastāñ śibirāñ jīvitaiṣiṇaḥ kṛtavarmā kṛpaś caiva dvāradeśe nijaghnatuḥ
english: But as those terrified men, longing for their lives, came rushing from the camp, Kṛtavarman and Kṛpa slew them at the gateway.

sanskrit: viśastrayantrakavacān muktakeśān kṛtāñjalīn vepamānān kṣitau bhītān naiva kāṃś cid amuñcatām
english: Disarmed, stripped of their gear and armor, their hair unbound, their palms joined in supplication, trembling and frightened upon the ground—not one of them did the two let go.

sanskrit: nāmucyata tayoḥ kaś cin niṣkrāntaḥ śibirād bahiḥ kṛpasya ca mahārāja hārdikyasya ca durmateḥ
english: Not one who came forth from the camp escaped the two, O great king—neither Kṛpa nor the malign-minded son of Hṛdika.

sanskrit: bhūyaś caiva cikīrṣantau droṇaputrasya tau priyam triṣu deśeṣu dadatuḥ śibirasya hutāśanam
english: And wishing to do still further pleasure to the son of Droṇa, the two set fire to the camp in three places.

sanskrit: tataḥ prakāśe śibire khaḍgena pitṛnandanaḥ aśvatthāmā mahārāja vyacarat kṛtahastavat
english: Then in the camp now lit bright, that delight of his father, Aśvatthāman, O great king, ranged about with his sword like a master of his craft.

sanskrit: kāṃś cid āpatato vīrān aparāṃś ca pradhāvataḥ vyayojayata khaḍgena prāṇair dvijavaro narān
english: Some heroes rushing upon him, others fleeing away—those men that best of the twice-born parted from their lives with his sword.

sanskrit: kāṃś cid yodhān sa khaḍgena madhye saṃchidya vīryavān apātayad droṇasutaḥ saṃrabdhas tilakāṇḍavat
english: Cleaving some warriors clean through the middle with his sword, the valiant son of Droṇa, in his fury, felled them as one cuts down stalks of sesame.

sanskrit: vinadadbhir bhṛśāyastair narāśvadviradottamaiḥ patitair abhavat kīrṇā medinī bharatarṣabha
english: With the finest of men, horses, and elephants—crying out, sorely afflicted, and fallen—the earth was strewn over, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: mānuṣāṇāṃ sahasreṣu hateṣu patiteṣu ca udatiṣṭhan kabandhāni bahūny utthāya cāpatan
english: As men were slain and fallen by the thousand, many headless trunks rose up, and having risen, fell again.

sanskrit: sāyudhān sāṅgadān bāhūn nicakarta śirāṃsi ca hastihastopamān ūrūn hastān pādāṃś ca bhārata
english: Arms still grasping weapons and bound with armlets he hewed off, and heads, and thighs like the trunks of elephants, and hands and feet, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhacchinnāñ śiraśchinnān pārśvacchinnāṃs tathāparān samāsādyākarod drauṇiḥ kāṃś cic cāpi parāṅmukhān
english: Some he made with their backs cleft, some with heads cleft, others with their sides cleft, did the son of Droṇa close in upon—and some he struck as they turned away.

sanskrit: madhyakāyān narān anyāṃś cicchedānyāṃś ca karṇataḥ aṃsadeśe nihatyānyān kāye prāveśayac chiraḥ
english: Some men he cut through the middle of the body, others he cleft from the ear, and striking still others upon the shoulder, he drove the head down into the trunk.

sanskrit: evaṃ vicaratas tasya nighnataḥ subahūn narān tamasā rajanī ghorā babhau dāruṇadarśanā
english: As he ranged about thus, slaying very many men, the dread night, dark and fearful to behold, shone over all.

sanskrit: kiṃ cit prāṇaiś ca puruṣair hataiś cānyaiḥ sahasraśaḥ bahunā ca gajāśvena bhūr abhūd bhīmadarśanā
english: With men yet barely breathing and others slain by the thousand, and with a multitude of elephants and horses, the earth became terrible to look upon.

sanskrit: yakṣarakṣaḥsamākīrṇe rathāśvadvipadāruṇe kruddhena droṇaputreṇa saṃchinnāḥ prāpatan bhuvi
english: In that ground thronged with yakṣas and rākṣasas, made dreadful with chariots, horses, and elephants, men hewn down by the wrathful son of Droṇa fell to the earth.

sanskrit: mātṝr anye pitṝn anye bhrātṝn anye vicukruśuḥ ke cid ūcur na tat kruddhair dhārtarāṣṭraiḥ kṛtaṃ raṇe
english: Some cried out for their mothers, some for their fathers, some for their brothers; and some said, "This was not done in battle by the angered sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: yat kṛtaṃ naḥ prasuptānāṃ rakṣobhiḥ krūrakarmabhiḥ asāṃnidhyād dhi pārthānām idaṃ naḥ kadanaṃ kṛtam
english: What has been wrought upon us as we slept was done by rākṣasas of cruel deeds; only because the Pārthas were not at hand has this slaughter been wrought upon us.

sanskrit: na devāsuragandharvair na yakṣair na ca rākṣasaiḥ śakyo vijetuṃ kaunteyo goptā yasya janārdanaḥ
english: Not by gods, asuras, or gandharvas, not by yakṣas nor by rākṣasas, can the son of Kuntī be conquered, whose protector is Janārdana.

sanskrit: brahmaṇyaḥ satyavāg dāntaḥ sarvabhūtānukampakaḥ na ca suptaṃ pramattaṃ vā nyastaśastraṃ kṛtāñjalim dhāvantaṃ muktakeśaṃ vā hanti pārtho dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Devoted to the Brahmins, truthful of speech, self-controlled, compassionate to all beings—never does Pārtha Dhanaṃjaya slay one who is asleep or off his guard, who has laid down his weapon, or joined his palms, or who runs with hair unbound."

sanskrit: tad idaṃ naḥ kṛtaṃ ghoraṃ rakṣobhiḥ krūrakarmabhiḥ iti lālapyamānāḥ sma śerate bahavo janāḥ
english: "This dreadful thing has been done to us by rākṣasas of cruel deeds"—thus lamenting, many men lay there dying.

sanskrit: stanatāṃ ca manuṣyāṇām apareṣāṃ ca kūjatām tato muhūrtāt prāśāmyat sa śabdas tumulo mahān
english: Of men groaning and of others moaning faintly—in a little while that great tumultuous clamor died away.

sanskrit: śoṇitavyatiṣiktāyāṃ vasudhāyāṃ ca bhūmipa tad rajas tumulaṃ ghoraṃ kṣaṇenāntaradhīyata
english: And as the earth was drenched all over with blood, O lord of the land, that thick and dreadful dust vanished in an instant.

sanskrit: saṃveṣṭamānān udvignān nirutsāhān sahasraśaḥ nyapātayan narān kruddhaḥ paśūn paśupatir yathā
english: Men writhing, panic-stricken, drained of spirit, by the thousand the wrathful one struck down, as the Lord of Beasts strikes down beasts.

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ saṃpariṣvajya śayānān dravato 'parān saṃlīnān yudhyamānāṃś ca sarvān drauṇir apothayat
english: Some lying clasped in one another's arms, others fleeing, some cowering in hiding, and some still fighting—all of them the son of Droṇa crushed.

sanskrit: dahyamānā hutāśena vadhyamānāś ca tena te parasparaṃ tadā yodhā anayan yamasādanam
english: Burning in the fire and slain by him, those warriors then sent one another to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: tasyā rajanyās tv ardhena pāṇḍavānāṃ mahad balam gamayām āsa rājendra drauṇir yamaniveśanam
english: Within the half of that single night, O lord of kings, the son of Droṇa sent the great host of the Pāṇḍavas to the dwelling of Yama.

sanskrit: niśācarāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ sa rātrir harṣavardhinī āsīn naragajāśvānāṃ raudrī kṣayakarī bhṛśam
english: To the creatures that roam by night that night was a swelling of joy, but to men, elephants, and horses it was savage and brought utter ruin.

sanskrit: tatrādṛśyanta rakṣāṃsi piśācāś ca pṛthagvidhāḥ khādanto naramāṃsāni pibantaḥ śoṇitāni ca
english: There were seen rākṣasas and piśācas of many kinds, devouring the flesh of men and drinking their blood.

sanskrit: karālāḥ piṅgalā raudrāḥ śailadantā rajasvalāḥ jaṭilā dīrghasakthāś ca pañcapādā mahodarāḥ
english: Gaping-mouthed, tawny-eyed, fierce, with teeth like crags, befouled with dust, matted-haired and long-thighed, five-footed and huge-bellied;

sanskrit: paścād aṅgulayo rūkṣā virūpā bhairavasvanāḥ ghaṭajānavo 'tihrasvāś ca nīlakaṇṭhā vibhīṣaṇāḥ
english: with fingers turned backward, harsh, misshapen, of fearful voice, with knees like pots, some very short, blue-throated and terrifying;

sanskrit: saputradārāḥ sukrūrā durdarśanasunirghṛṇāḥ vividhāni ca rūpāṇi tatrādṛśyanta rakṣasām
english: with their wives and children, exceedingly cruel, hideous to behold and pitiless—forms of every kind among the rākṣasas were seen there.

sanskrit: pītvā ca śoṇitaṃ hṛṣṭāḥ prānṛtyan gaṇaśo 'pare idaṃ varam idaṃ medhyam idaṃ svādv iti cābruvan
english: Others, having drunk blood, danced in rejoicing bands, and cried, "This is choice, this is pure, this is sweet!"

sanskrit: medomajjāsthiraktānāṃ vasānāṃ ca bhṛśāsitāḥ paramāṃsāni khādantaḥ kravyādā māṃsajīvinaḥ
english: Greedy for fat, marrow, bone, blood, and entrails, the eaters of carrion, who live upon flesh, gorged on the choicest meats.

sanskrit: vasāṃ cāpy apare pītvā paryadhāvan vikukṣilāḥ nānāvaktrās tathā raudrāḥ kravyādāḥ piśitāśinaḥ
english: Others, having drunk the marrow-grease, ran about with bellies swollen, those fierce, many-faced eaters of carrion and devourers of flesh.

sanskrit: ayutāni ca tatrāsan prayutāny arbudāni ca rakṣasāṃ ghorarūpāṇāṃ mahatāṃ krūrakarmaṇām
english: By tens of thousands they were there, by hundreds of thousands and by tens of millions—rākṣasas of dreadful form, vast and cruel in their deeds.

sanskrit: muditānāṃ vitṛptānāṃ tasmin mahati vaiśase sametāni bahūny āsan bhūtāni ca janādhipa
english: Rejoicing and well sated in that great carnage, many such beings gathered there together, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: pratyūṣakāle śibirāt pratigantum iyeṣa saḥ nṛśoṇitāvasiktasya drauṇer āsīd asitsaruḥ pāṇinā saha saṃśliṣṭa ekībhūta iva prabho
english: At the hour before dawn he wished to depart from the camp; and of the son of Droṇa, drenched in the blood of men, the hilt of his sword clung to his hand, become as one with it, O lord.

sanskrit: sa niḥśeṣān arīn kṛtvā virarāja janakṣaye yugānte sarvabhūtāni bhasma kṛtveva pāvakaḥ
english: Having left not one foe remaining, he shone amid the slaughter of men, like the fire at the end of an age when it has reduced all beings to ashes.

sanskrit: yathāpratijñaṃ tat karma kṛtvā drauṇāyaniḥ prabho durgamāṃ padavīṃ kṛtvā pitur āsīd gatajvaraḥ
english: Having done that deed according to his vow, O lord, and having trodden the path his father had walked, the son of Droṇa became freed of his fever.

sanskrit: yathaiva saṃsuptajane śibire prāviśan niśi tathaiva hatvā niḥśabde niścakrāma nararṣabhaḥ
english: Even as he had entered the camp by night while its folk lay asleep, so, having slain them in silence, that bull among men came forth again.

sanskrit: niṣkramya śibirāt tasmāt tābhyāṃ saṃgamya vīryavān ācakhyau karma tat sarvaṃ hṛṣṭaḥ saṃharṣayan vibho
english: Coming forth from that camp and meeting with the two, the valiant one recounted all that deed in joy, gladdening them, O lord.

sanskrit: tāv apy ācakhyatus tasmai priyaṃ priyakarau tadā pāñcālān sṛñjayāṃś caiva vinikṛttān sahasraśaḥ prītyā coccair udakrośaṃs tathaivāsphoṭayaṃs talān
english: And the two, who had done him a kindness, told him in turn a welcome thing then—of Pāñcālas and Sṛñjayas cut down by the thousand—and in their delight they cried aloud and clapped their hands.

sanskrit: evaṃvidhā hi sā rātriḥ somakānāṃ janakṣaye prasuptānāṃ pramattānām āsīt subhṛśadāruṇā
english: Such, then, was that night in the slaughter of the Somakas—for those who slept off their guard it was exceedingly terrible.

sanskrit: asaṃśayaṃ hi kālasya paryāyo duratikramaḥ tādṛśā nihatā yatra kṛtvāsmākaṃ janakṣayam
english: Beyond doubt the turning of Time is hard to overpass, since such men as these were slain there—they who had wrought the slaughter of our own host.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca prāg eva sumahat karma drauṇir etan mahārathaḥ nākarod īdṛśaṃ kasmān matputravijaye dhṛtaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Why did the son of Droṇa, that great chariot-warrior, not do this so mighty deed long before, bent as he was on my sons' victory?

sanskrit: atha kasmād dhate kṣatre karmedaṃ kṛtavān asau droṇaputro maheṣvāsas tan me śaṃsitum arhasi
english: And why was it only after the warrior class was destroyed that the son of Droṇa, that great archer, wrought this deed? This you must tell me.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca teṣāṃ nūnaṃ bhayān nāsau kṛtavān kurunandana asāṃnidhyād dhi pārthānāṃ keśavasya ca dhīmataḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Surely it was for fear of them that he did not do it before, O delight of the Kurus—only in the absence of the Pārthas and of wise Keśava.

sanskrit: sātyakeś cāpi karmedaṃ droṇaputreṇa sādhitam na hi teṣāṃ samakṣaṃ tān hanyād api marutpatiḥ
english: And of Sātyaki too: this deed was accomplished by the son of Droṇa only in their absence—for in their sight not even the lord of the Maruts could have slain them.

sanskrit: etad īdṛśakaṃ vṛttaṃ rājan suptajane vibho tato janakṣayaṃ kṛtvā pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātyayam diṣṭyā diṣṭyeti cānyonyaṃ sametyocur mahārathāḥ
english: Such was the deed that befell while the folk lay asleep, O king, O lord; and having wrought this great destruction of the Pāṇḍavas, those great chariot-warriors met and said to one another, "By fortune! By fortune!"

sanskrit: paryaṣvajat tato drauṇis tābhyāṃ ca pratinanditaḥ idaṃ harṣāc ca sumahad ādade vākyam uttamam
english: Then the son of Droṇa embraced the two and was hailed by them in return, and out of his joy he spoke this lofty and excellent word:

sanskrit: pāñcālā nihatāḥ sarve draupadeyāś ca sarvaśaḥ somakā matsyaśeṣāś ca sarve vinihatā mayā
english: "The Pāñcālas are all slain, and the sons of Draupadī every one; the Somakas, and what remained of the Matsyas—all have been struck down by me.

sanskrit: idānīṃ kṛtakṛtyāḥ sma yāma tatraiva māciram yadi jīvati no rājā tasmai śaṃsāmahe priyam
english: Now our task is accomplished. Let us go yonder without delay; if our king yet lives, we shall tell him this welcome news."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca te hatvā sarvapāñcālān draupadeyāṃś ca sarvaśaḥ agacchan sahitās tatra yatra duryodhano hataḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Having slain all the Pāñcālas and the sons of Draupadī every one, they went together to where Duryodhana lay struck down.

sanskrit: gatvā cainam apaśyaṃs te kiṃ cit prāṇaṃ narādhipam tato rathebhyaḥ praskandya parivavrus tavātmajam
english: And going there they saw that lord of men still barely breathing; then, leaping down from their chariots, they gathered round your son.

sanskrit: taṃ bhagnasakthaṃ rājendra kṛcchraprāṇam acetasam vamantaṃ rudhiraṃ vaktrād apaśyan vasudhātale
english: Him with thighs broken, O lord of kings, his breath labored and his senses gone, vomiting blood from his mouth, they beheld upon the ground.

sanskrit: vṛtaṃ samantād bahubhiḥ śvāpadair ghoradarśanaiḥ śālāvṛkagaṇaiś caiva bhakṣayiṣyadbhir antikāt
english: Hemmed about on every side by many beasts of prey, dreadful to behold, and by packs of jackals drawing near to devour him.

sanskrit: nivārayantaṃ kṛcchrāt tāñ śvāpadān saṃcikhādiṣūn viveṣṭamānaṃ mahyāṃ ca subhṛśaṃ gāḍhavedanam
english: With great difficulty warding off those beasts that strove to devour him, writhing upon the earth in deep and grievous pain.

sanskrit: taṃ śayānaṃ mahātmānaṃ bhūmau svarudhirokṣitam hataśiṣṭās trayo vīrāḥ śokārtāḥ paryavārayan aśvatthāmā kṛpaś caiva kṛtavarmā ca sātvataḥ
english: That great-souled one lying upon the ground, bathed in his own blood, the three surviving heroes, stricken with grief, gathered round—Aśvatthāman, Kṛpa, and Kṛtavarman of the Sātvata line.

sanskrit: tais tribhiḥ śoṇitādigdhair niḥśvasadbhir mahārathaiḥ śuśubhe saṃvṛto rājā vedī tribhir ivāgnibhiḥ
english: Encircled by those three great chariot-warriors, smeared with blood and sighing heavily, the king shone like an altar set about with three fires.

sanskrit: te taṃ śayānaṃ saṃprekṣya rājānam atathocitam aviṣahyena duḥkhena tatas te rurudus trayaḥ
english: Beholding the king lying so, in a state he had never deserved, the three, in grief past all bearing, then wept aloud.

sanskrit: tatas te rudhiraṃ hastair mukhān nirmṛjya tasya ha raṇe rājñaḥ śayānasya kṛpaṇaṃ paryadevayan
english: Then, wiping the blood from his face with their hands, they lamented piteously over the king who lay there upon the field.

sanskrit: kṛpa uvāca na daivasyātibhāro 'sti yad ayaṃ rudhirokṣitaḥ ekādaśacamūbhartā śete duryodhano hataḥ
english: Kṛpa said: For fate there is no burden too great, since this Duryodhana, lord of eleven armies, lies slain and bathed in blood.

sanskrit: paśya cāmīkarābhasya cāmīkaravibhūṣitām gadāṃ gadāpriyasyemāṃ samīpe patitāṃ bhuvi
english: Behold, beside him who shone like gold and was adorned with gold, his mace—the mace he loved—fallen here upon the ground close by.

sanskrit: iyam enaṃ gadā śūraṃ na jahāti raṇe raṇe svargāyāpi vrajantaṃ hi na jahāti yaśasvinam
english: This mace forsook not the hero in battle after battle, and now, as the renowned one passes even to heaven, it does not forsake him.

sanskrit: paśyemāṃ saha vīreṇa jāmbūnadavibhūṣitām śayānāṃ śayane dharme bhāryāṃ prītimatīm iva
english: Behold it, adorned with gold from the Jambū river, lying beside the hero on the bed of righteousness, like a loving wife at his side.

sanskrit: yo vai mūrdhāvasiktānām agre yātaḥ paraṃtapaḥ sa hato grasate pāṃsūn paśya kālasya paryayam
english: He who, the scorcher of foes, marched at the head of anointed kings—he, now slain, swallows the dust. Behold the turning of Time!

sanskrit: yenājau nihatā bhūmāv aśerata purā dviṣaḥ sa bhūmau nihataḥ śete kururājaḥ parair ayam
english: He by whom in battle the foe were once struck down to lie upon the earth—this king of the Kurus, slain by his enemies, now himself lies upon the earth.

sanskrit: bhayān namanti rājāno yasya sma śatasaṃghaśaḥ sa vīraśayane śete kravyādbhiḥ parivāritaḥ
english: He before whom kings by the hundredfold bowed down in fear—he lies upon the hero's bed, ringed about by eaters of carrion.

sanskrit: upāsata nṛpāḥ pūrvam arthahetor yam īśvaram dhik sadyo nihataḥ śete paśya kālasya paryayam
english: That lord whom kings once attended for the sake of gain—alas! struck down in a moment he lies. Behold the turning of Time!

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca taṃ śayānaṃ nṛpaśreṣṭhaṃ tato bharatasattama aśvatthāmā samālokya karuṇaṃ paryadevayat
english: Saṃjaya said: Then, O best of the Bharatas, looking upon that foremost of kings as he lay there, Aśvatthāman lamented piteously.

sanskrit: āhus tvāṃ rājaśārdūla mukhyaṃ sarvadhanuṣmatām dhanādhyakṣopamaṃ yuddhe śiṣyaṃ saṃkarṣaṇasya ha
english: They called you, O tiger among kings, the foremost of all bowmen, in battle the peer of the Lord of Wealth, the pupil of Saṃkarṣaṇa himself.

sanskrit: kathaṃ vivaram adrākṣīd bhīmasenas tavānagha balinaḥ kṛtino nityaṃ sa ca pāpātmavān nṛpa
english: How did Bhīmasena spy an opening in you, O blameless one—in you who were ever mighty and accomplished—that base-souled wretch, O king?

sanskrit: kālo nūnaṃ mahārāja loke 'smin balavattaraḥ paśyāmo nihataṃ tvāṃ ced bhīmasenena saṃyuge
english: Surely, O great king, Time is the stronger power in this world, since we see you struck down by Bhīmasena in the fray.

sanskrit: kathaṃ tvāṃ sarvadharmajñaṃ kṣudraḥ pāpo vṛkodaraḥ nikṛtyā hatavān mando nūnaṃ kālo duratyayaḥ
english: How could the base, wicked, and sluggish Vṛkodara, by foul trickery, have slain you who knew all the laws of righteousness? Surely Time is past overcoming.

sanskrit: dharmayuddhe hy adharmeṇa samāhūyaujasā mṛdhe gadayā bhīmasenena nirbhinne sakthinī tava
english: For in a fair fight, by unfair means, called out by him with force in the press of battle, your two thighs were shattered by Bhīmasena's mace.

sanskrit: adharmeṇa hatasyājau mṛdyamānaṃ padā śiraḥ yad upekṣitavān kṣudro dhik tam astu yudhiṣṭhiram
english: And as your head, you slain by unfair means in battle, was being trampled under his foot—that the base one looked on and let it be: shame, then, upon that Yudhiṣṭhira!
